summary: Modern databases have evolved beyond storage and query engines to become first-class AI platforms, embedding vector search, LLM orchestration, and ML model inference directly into the data layer. This shift eliminates the need to move data to external AI infrastructure, reducing latency, governance risk, and operational complexity. By 2026, with 75% of enterprise AI applications depending on vector search and vector database adoption growing 377% year-over-year, in-database AI capabilities have become a primary evaluation criterion for data platform selection.

databases.name: Snowflake (Cortex AI)
databases.description: Cortex AI provides a suite of serverless AI functions natively inside Snowflake, including text-to-SQL, summarization, sentiment analysis, translation, and embedding generation via COMPLETE, EMBED_TEXT, SUMMARIZE, and SENTIMENT functions. Snowflake Postgres (GA soon as of early 2026) runs natively in the AI Data Cloud and integrates pgvector for vector similarity search alongside Cortex AI functions, enabling full RAG pipelines without leaving the platform. Cortex also supports fine-tuned and hosted LLMs including Mistral, LLaMA, and Snowflake Arctic, with enterprise governance and data mirroring for analytics and AI processing.
databases.llm_integration: Supports hosted open-source LLMs (Mistral, LLaMA 3, Snowflake Arctic, Reka) via Cortex COMPLETE function; integrates with Snowflake Postgres and pgvector for embedding storage and similarity search; text-to-SQL and embedding generation built in natively.
databases.pricing_notes: Cortex AI functions are billed per token consumed, on top of standard Snowflake compute credits. Snowflake Postgres pricing follows compute and storage tiers. Enterprise contracts typically bundle credits; costs can scale significantly at high LLM call volumes. No separate licensing fee for Cortex functions beyond credit consumption.

databases.name: Google BigQuery (BigQuery ML + Vertex AI)
databases.ai_feature: BigQuery ML and Vertex AI Integration
databases.description: BigQuery ML allows data teams to create and execute ML models using standard SQL syntax directly on BigQuery tables, supporting linear regression, logistic regression, k-means clustering, matrix factorization, boosted trees (XGBoost), AutoML Tables, and deep neural networks. BigQuery is deeply integrated with Vertex AI, enabling users to call Vertex AI hosted LLMs including Gemini models directly from SQL using the ML.GENERATE_TEXT and ML.EMBED_TEXT functions. Vector search is supported natively via BigQuery Vector Search, allowing approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) search over embedding columns stored in BigQuery tables, suitable for RAG workloads at scale.
databases.llm_integration: Native integration with Google Vertex AI and Gemini models (Gemini 1.5 Pro, Flash, and others) via ML.GENERATE_TEXT and ML.EMBED_TEXT SQL functions; supports remote model endpoints; enables embedding generation, summarization, classification, and grounding directly in SQL queries against BigQuery data.
databases.pricing_notes: BigQuery ML model training and inference are charged separately from standard BigQuery query costs. ML.GENERATE_TEXT and ML.EMBED_TEXT calls are billed at Vertex AI API rates passed through BigQuery. BigQuery Vector Search is included within standard BigQuery compute pricing. On-demand and flat-rate (slot reservation) pricing models apply. Costs can accumulate quickly with large-scale LLM inference jobs.

databases.name: PostgreSQL (pgvector + pgai)
databases.description: pgvector is an open-source PostgreSQL extension that adds a native vector data type and similarity search operators (L2, cosine, inner product) to standard PostgreSQL instances, enabling storage and querying of embeddings from any model alongside relational data. It supports IVFFlat and HNSW indexing for approximate nearest neighbor search and handles up to 50 million vectors comfortably for RAG workloads as of 2026. pgai (developed by Timescale) extends this further by adding SQL functions to call embedding APIs (OpenAI, Cohere, Ollama) and LLMs directly from within PostgreSQL, enabling full AI pipelines without leaving the database. pgvector integrates natively with Snowflake Postgres and Databricks environments.
databases.llm_integration: pgai extension enables direct calls to OpenAI, Cohere, Anthropic, and Ollama LLM APIs from SQL functions inside PostgreSQL; supports embedding generation, completion, and classification natively in SQL; pgvector handles storage and ANN retrieval of resulting embeddings.
databases.pricing_notes: pgvector and pgai are both open-source and free to use on self-hosted PostgreSQL. Managed offerings with pgvector included (Supabase, Neon, Tembo, AWS RDS, Google Cloud SQL, Azure Database for PostgreSQL) are billed at standard managed database compute and storage rates. LLM API calls made via pgai are billed directly by the respective LLM provider (e.g., OpenAI per-token pricing). No licensing fees for extensions themselves.

databases.name: Amazon (Aurora ML + Redshift ML)
databases.description: Aurora ML integrates Amazon Aurora (MySQL and PostgreSQL-compatible) with Amazon SageMaker and Amazon Comprehend, enabling SQL-based invocation of ML model endpoints for inference directly within database queries, covering use cases like sentiment analysis, fraud detection, and classification. Redshift ML allows Amazon Redshift users to create, train, and deploy ML models using SQL via integration with SageMaker AutoPilot, supporting classification, regression, and time-series forecasting. Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL-compatible edition also supports pgvector for vector similarity search, providing a managed path to embedding storage and RAG pipelines within the AWS ecosystem. Amazon Bedrock integration further extends LLM access from within AWS data services.
databases.llm_integration: Aurora ML integrates with Amazon SageMaker endpoints and Amazon Bedrock for LLM inference; Redshift ML uses SageMaker AutoPilot for model training; pgvector on Aurora PostgreSQL enables embedding-based RAG workflows; Bedrock provides access to Anthropic Claude, Amazon Titan, Meta LLaMA, and other foundational models callable from application layers connected to Aurora or Redshift.
databases.pricing_notes: Aurora ML and Redshift ML incur costs for the underlying Aurora or Redshift instance plus SageMaker inference endpoint costs billed separately per hour and per invocation. Bedrock API calls are billed per token by model. pgvector on Aurora PostgreSQL has no additional extension cost beyond standard Aurora instance pricing. Total cost of ownership can be complex to predict given multiple AWS service meters.

databases.name: Databricks (MLflow + DBRX)
databases.ai_feature: Databricks AI — MLflow, DBRX, Mosaic AI, and Vector Search
databases.description: Databricks provides a comprehensive in-platform AI layer through Mosaic AI (formerly Databricks ML), which includes MLflow for experiment tracking, model registry, and deployment; DBRX as Databricks' own open-source LLM; and Databricks Vector Search for storing and querying embeddings natively within the Databricks Lakehouse. The platform supports full RAG pipeline construction with Delta tables as the source, automatic embedding generation via Foundation Model APIs, and retrieval via managed vector indexes. Databricks integrates with pgvector in external Postgres environments and serves as a data mirror and AI processing layer for Snowflake Postgres per Snowflake's own documentation. Unity Catalog provides governance across models, embeddings, and data assets.
databases.llm_integration: Supports DBRX, Meta LLaMA, Mistral, and other open-source LLMs via Mosaic AI Foundation Model APIs; integrates with external LLM providers via MLflow AI Gateway; enables LLM-based pipelines with LangChain, LlamaIndex, and custom agents natively on the platform; Unity Catalog governs model and embedding access.
databases.pricing_notes: Databricks is priced on Databricks Units (DBUs) consumed by compute clusters and serverless endpoints. Vector Search is billed on DBUs for indexing and querying operations. Foundation Model API calls (including DBRX) are billed per token at published rates. MLflow is open-source and free; managed MLflow on Databricks is included in platform subscriptions. Enterprise pricing is negotiated; can be cost-efficient at scale with reserved capacity.

databases.name: MongoDB Atlas Vector Search
databases.description: MongoDB Atlas Vector Search enables storage and querying of vector embeddings directly within MongoDB Atlas collections alongside operational document data, using approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) search powered by Lucene's HNSW implementation. It supports pre-filtering by any document field before vector search, enabling highly selective hybrid search over structured metadata and semantic embeddings in a single query. Atlas integrates with major embedding providers and LLM frameworks including LangChain, LlamaIndex, OpenAI, and Amazon Bedrock, making it a full RAG backend within a general-purpose document database. Atlas also offers Atlas Search for lexical queries and is listed among the top 15 vector databases for production RAG workloads in 2026.
databases.llm_integration: Integrates natively with OpenAI, Anthropic, Amazon Bedrock, Azure OpenAI, Google Vertex AI, Cohere, and Hugging Face via LangChain and LlamaIndex connectors; Atlas Data API allows LLM agents to retrieve and store documents; no proprietary LLM but full orchestration support for external providers.
databases.pricing_notes: Atlas Vector Search is available on M10 dedicated clusters and above; not available on free or shared tiers. Pricing is based on Atlas cluster size (compute and storage) with no separate per-query fee for vector search. Costs scale with cluster tier and data volume. Serverless Atlas instances do not support Vector Search as of 2026. Managed fully by MongoDB with multi-cloud support across AWS, GCP, and Azure.
